messages.author: b16a5af9e10063ea
messages.subject: quantile regression help
parts:
Hi everyone,

First off apologies if this a massively naive series of questions, I have googled and read everything I can find but am at a loss:

I (think) I want to run a quantile regression on some spatially count data. I have non linear relationships in my data with a triangular (i.e. reduction in variance type patterna) for several of the covariates.

I have been reading Yue & Rue 2009 but confess I am not at the level where I can understand much of the technical side of it. Effectively I want to recreate table five from that paper where I can see the slope estimate for different quantiles e.g. 5, 25, 50, 75, 95

I ran the example code from the study:

   library(INLA)
   data(Munich)
   g = system.file("demodata/munich.graph", package="INLA")
   formula = rent ~ f(location,model="besag",graph.file=g,param=c(1,.001)) +
   f(year,model="crw2",values=seq(1918,2001),param=c(1,.001)) +
   f(floor.size,model="crw2",param=c(1,.001)) + 
   Gute.Wohnlage + Beste.Wohnlage + Keine.Wwv + Keine.Zh +
   Kein.Badkach + Besond.Bad + Gehobene.Kueche +
   zim1 + zim2 + zim3 + zim4 + zim5 + zim6 -1
   mod = inla(formula,data = Munich, verbose = T, family = "laplace",
   control.data=list(alpha=.5, gamma=2, epsilon=.01),
   control.predictor = list(initial = 12), control.inla = list(h=1e-4))

and got the following error message:

     Error in inla(formula, data = Munich, verbose = T, family = "laplace",  : 
     unused argument (control.data = list(alpha = 0.5, gamma = 2, epsilon = 0.01))

Has this functionality been superseded/removed? Have I missed something? Also I am not sure where you specify the quantiles and I do fully understand what 'control.predictor' and 'control.inla' are doing here.

Again I am sorry if this is naive.

Thanks very much for your help,
Dave

I believe the options are the same, so it might run correctly if you
just change the name of the argument.
